body: Data quality research has usually treated data as an input that is stored, processed, and validated. In AI-driven software-intensive systems, data also shapes model behavior, evaluation, and lawful use. Empirical evidence remains limited on how practitioners define, assess, and manage quality under these conditions. We interviewed 16 practitioners from nine organizations and analyzed the transcripts using reflexive thematic analysis and developed six themes from participants' accounts. In AI systems, traceability shifted from modular debugging to attributing model behavior, while using models as quality assessors introduced circularity. Agent context and memory became data objects, and synthetic and pseudo-labeled data made authenticity a quality concern. In foundation-model development, lawfulness became a gate for training data, while representativeness was judged through coverage of situations in which the system must behave safely. Prior ML research examines many of these problems separately. Our study provides a practitioner-grounded account of how they are encountered together as an engineering and organizational concern. We also interpret five recurring conditions as helping explain how the themes relate to reduced trust in data and AI outcomes. We synthesize these findings through lifecycle assurance: a conceptual framing focused on producing evidence that data can support a specific AI claim when its influence may be embedded in model behavior, model-based judgments, or agent actions.
summaryZh: 数据质量研究通常将数据视为静态输入，但在AI软件密集型系统中，数据还会塑造模型行为、评估和合法性。本研究通过对来自9个组织的16位从业者进行访谈，归纳出六大主题：追溯性转变为归因模型行为、模型作为评估者引入循环性、智能体上下文与内存成为数据对象、合成数据引发真实性担忧等。研究最终将这些发现综合为生命周期assurance框架。

glossary.explanationZh: 生命周期保障，专注于证明数据在整个AI系统生命周期中支持特定声明的框架
基于模型的判断，使用大模型本身作为裁判或评估工具来辅助系统验证的做法
智能体上下文，作为动态数据对象参与智能体长期记忆和决策的环境信息
合成数据，由AI模型生成用于训练或微调的模拟数据
